task.title: Device Cannot Connect
task.shortdesc: Identify and correct conditions that prevent a client device from connecting to the wired or wireless network.

prereq.p: Before you troubleshoot the connection, make sure that:

ul.li: The status indicators on the router show normal operation.
The primary Wi-Fi network is configured.
You have access to the network settings on the client device.
You have recorded recent changes to the router or client device.

prereq.note: Make one change at a time. Test the connection after each change.

context.p: A client device can fail to connect because of an incorrect network name or password, an unsupported security mode, weak signal strength, disabled network hardware, incorrect IP settings, or an access restriction.
First, determine whether the problem affects one device or multiple devices. Then, check the applicable wired or wireless connection.
context.note: Wi-Fi passwords are case-sensitive. Enter uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters exactly as configured.
Record the authentication result, assigned network settings, connected access point, signal information, and relevant router events before you change the configuration.

step.cmd: Determine which devices cannot connect.

substep.cmd: Try to connect another client device to the same network.
If available, test one wired device and one wireless device.
Record which devices and connection types are affected.

ul.li: If only one device is affected, check that client device and its saved network settings.
If all wireless devices are affected, check the Wi-Fi configuration on the router.
If all wired devices are affected, check the Ethernet cables and LAN ports.
If all devices are affected, check the router, power connection, and network configuration.

step.stepresult: The scope of the connection problem is identified.

step.cmd: Identify the connection type used by the affected device.

choices.choice: For a wireless device, continue with the Wi-Fi checks.
For a wired device, continue with the Ethernet checks.

step.cmd: Make sure that Wi-Fi is enabled on the wireless device.

info.p: Turn off airplane mode if airplane mode disables Wi-Fi on the device.
Turn Wi-Fi off and then turn Wi-Fi on again.

step.cmd: Confirm that the device can detect .

info.p: Move the client device closer to the if the network does not appear in the list of available Wi-Fi networks.
Confirm that the router Wi-Fi indicator shows normal operation.
info.note: Make sure that the device does not select unless the device must use the guest network.

step.cmd: Enter the current .

info.p: Make sure that you enter all characters correctly.
info.note: Do not use the password for the as the Wi-Fi password.
If the password is not visible while you enter it, use the password-display control when this control is available. Make sure that other persons cannot see the password.

step.cmd: Remove the saved Wi-Fi network from the client device.

substep.cmd: Open the Wi-Fi settings on the client device.
Select .
Select the control to forget or remove the network.
Select again.
Enter the current .
Try to connect again.

info.note: Make sure that you know the current Wi-Fi password before you remove the saved network.

step.stepresult: The client device creates a new Wi-Fi connection profile.

step.cmd: Check the Wi-Fi signal strength.

substep.cmd: Move the client device closer to the .
Try to connect again.

info.p: If the device connects near the router, distance, interference, or a physical obstruction can prevent the connection in the original location.
For more information, see .

step.cmd: Test another supported Wi-Fi band.

choices.choice: Use the 2.4 GHz band if the device does not support 5 GHz or is far from the router.
Use the 5 GHz band if the device supports 5 GHz and is near the router.

info.p: The supports .
info.note: Some IoT devices support only the 2.4 GHz band.
info.p: For more information, see .

step.cmd: Confirm that the client device supports the configured security mode.

info.p: The wireless network in this guide uses .
If an older device does not support WPA3, use WPA2/WPA3 transition mode when this option is available.
info.note: Do not use WEP or another obsolete security protocol to connect an old device.
info.p: For more information, see .

step.cmd: Check the Ethernet connection for a wired device.

substep.cmd: Make sure that the Ethernet cable is fully connected to the client device.
Make sure that the other end of the cable is connected to an available LAN port.
Check the cable and its connectors for visible damage.
Replace the cable with a known working cable if necessary.
Connect the cable to another compatible LAN port if one is available.

info.p: You can use if the port is available.

step.stepresult: The wired device has a working physical connection to the router.

step.cmd: Check the Ethernet switch if the device connects through a switch.

info.p: Make sure that the switch is turned on and connected to the .
Check the applicable port indicators and Ethernetcables.
Connect the client device directly to the router to determine whether the switch causes the problem.

step.cmd: Restart the affected client device.

info.p: After the restart, enable the required network connection and try to connect again.

step.cmd: Restart the router if multiple devices are affected.

substep.cmd: Use the restart control in the if this control is available.
Wait until the router status indicators show normal operation.
Try to connect the affected device again.

info.note: Do not press the reset button. A factory reset can remove the custom network configuration.

step.cmd: Review the connected-device list in the .

substep.cmd: Go to .
Sign in with the credentials for the .
Open the .
Open the connected-device list.
Check whether the affected device appears in the list.

info.p: The device can appear by its device name, IP address, or MAC address.
info.note: Some devices use private or randomized MAC addresses. Compare the displayed address with the address in the device network settings.

step.cmd: Confirm that the client device is not blocked.

info.p: Review the blocked-device list, access-control list, and parental control settings in the .
Remove the device from the blocked list only if the device is authorized.
info.note: Verify the device name and MAC address before you change an access-control setting.

step.cmd: Review the guest network restrictions if the device uses .

info.p: Confirm that the guest network is enabled and within its configured operating schedule.
Confirm that the maximum number of guest devices has not been reached.
Guest devices can have Internet access without access to the primary network or the .

step.cmd: Check whether the network device limit has been reached.

info.p: Review the number of connected devices on the .
Disconnect devices that are no longer required. Then, try to connect the affected device again.
info.note: Do not disconnect or block a device until you confirm that the device is not required.

step.cmd: Verify the network settings on the client device.

substep.cmd: Confirm that the device has a valid address.
Confirm that the subnet mask is .
Confirm that the default gateway is .
Confirm that a valid DNS server address is assigned.

info.p: If the device uses automatic configuration, the typically assigns an address from .
info.note: The network settings can differ if an administrator changed the default configuration.

step.cmd: Enable automatic IP address and DNS assignment on the client device.

info.p: Use automatic configuration unless the network requires a manually configured address.
Disconnect and reconnect the network interface after you change the address settings.

step.cmd: Check for an IP address conflict.

info.p: Confirm that another client device does not use the same IP address.
Do not manually assign if the can assign the same address from .
Use a DHCP reservation or an approved address outside the dynamic assignment range when a fixed address is required.

step.cmd: Review the wireless authentication events.

info.p: Review available router events for authentication, association, and security-mode failures.
Look for the following conditions:
info.note: Do not share logs that contain passwords, access tokens, private keys, or other confidential information.

step.cmd: Check the access point or mesh node if the device does not connect directly to the main router.

info.p: Confirm that the or is online.
Confirm that the wireless coverage point uses the correct SSID and compatible security settings.
Move a wireless mesh node closer to the main router or another connected node if its backhaul connection is weak.
For more information, see .

step.cmd: Check for updates for the client device.

info.p: Install approved operating-system, Wi-Fi adapter, Ethernet adapter, and device firmware updates.
Restart the client device if the update procedure requires a restart.

step.cmd: Check for an approved firmware update for the .

info.p: Use the update function in the or get approved firmware from the .
info.note: Do not turn off the router during a firmware update.
Install only firmware intended for and the applicable .

step.cmd: Verify the client-device connection.

substep.cmd: Connect the device through Ethernet or .
Confirm that the device shows an active network connection.
Open a supported web browser.
Go to and confirm that the router sign-in page opens.
Open a trusted external website.
Confirm that the website opens without a connection error.

step.stepresult: The client device can access the local network and Internet services.

result.p: The client device is connected to the through Ethernet or Wi-Fi. The device can access the local network and Internet services.

postreq.p: If the client device still cannot connect, collect the following information:

ul.li: The client IP configuration, authentication events, signal information, and access-control status

postreq.note: Do not send Wi-Fi passwords, administrator passwords, account passwords, access tokens, or other confidential credentials to technical support.
postreq.p: Contact the through an approved support channel. For more information, go to .
